question: A thousand less: is that per month or per year?
moment: Carver is about a thousand less. Which is a lot. That is, I mean, that is real money.

notes.title: Choosing between the Carver Street and park apartments
notes.summary: The speaker has to answer by Monday and is choosing between the cheap apartment on Carver Street and the pricier one by the park. Carver is about a thousand less a month, roughly $12,000 a year, but is fifty-five minutes door to door each way, versus about twelve minutes on foot from the park one. They framed it as literally a trade of money versus time. They worked out that Carver adds forty-three minutes each way: eighty-six minutes a day, seven and a half hours a week, and about three hundred and sixty hours a year. That comes to roughly thirty-three dollars an hour 'to not be on a bus.' Put that way, it sounded reasonable to them ('I think I would pay that'), but they did not make a decision.

openThreads.text: They still have to choose between the cheap Carver Street apartment and the one by the park, and the answer is due Monday.
Whether paying about thirty-three dollars an hour to not be on a bus is worth it: 'I think I would pay that,' but it is not settled.
